solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Friend in capital embracing daughter — Hannah, perhaps

indicators.note: embracing here just signals that the daughter is held close up against the capital, side by side

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A friend in some capital city is putting their arms round a daughter called Hannah.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannah reads the same in both directions, which is why it is offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah is a name spelt identically forwards and backwards, the textbook kind of word that reads both ways.

clue.text: Page in South America chart turned up, showing these?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. reversed
in places the page letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a map is a chart

explanation.surface: A map of South America is held up to show some feature of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads the letters upwards. 'these' points back to what such a South American map would show, so the clue edges towards &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of Argentina, exactly what a South American map displays.

clue.text: What's left, for example, with decorative trimming around

indicators.note: around means the lacy letters go round the example abbreviation

parts.note: lacy describes something with decorative lace trimming
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone describes an inheritance, perhaps an old garment, with ornamental edging.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is what a deceased person leaves behind in a will to their heirs.

clue.text: Country air that'll get you back on your feet?

definitions.text: Country air that'll get you back on your feet?

parts.words: Country air that'll get you back on your feet?
parts.note: country air sounds like a rural health cure, but it is a nation's tune, and audiences stand when it is played

explanation.walkthrough: Country air suggests fresh air in the countryside helping recovery; really it is the tune of a country, for which everyone rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nation has its official song, and custom requires people to stand up while it is played.

clue.text: Competition in which three good passes help team achieve winning goal

definitions.text: Competition in which three good passes help team achieve winning goal

parts.words: Competition in which three good passes help team achieve winning goal
parts.note: passes sound like football, but in a four-runner race the baton is handed over three times

explanation.walkthrough: Passes and team suggest football; a four-person team running in turn passes a baton three times before the finish line.
explanation.definitionFit: In this athletics event four runners each cover one leg, handing a baton on three times before the finish.

clue.text: Old boy in charge is overexcited

parts.note: old boy is an informal term for a man

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow given responsibility gets far too worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frenzied, wildly agitated behaviour, an extreme state of excitement.

clue.text: Magazine's back issue

indicators.note: back means the magazine's name is read the other way round

parts.note: Time is a well-known news magazine

explanation.surface: It sounds like a request for an old back issue of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back issue' looks like one phrase; 'back' reverses TIME, and 'issue' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or send forth, as when a chimney issues smoke.

clue.text: Rebuilt a Metro line around Northern French city, originally

indicators.note: around places the rebuilt letters about the northern abbreviation
rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's underground line is reconstructed round a northern district.
explanation.walkthrough: Montreal was founded as a French colonial settlement, hence 'originally'; it is now in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreal began as Ville-Marie in New France, so it was a French city in its origins and still speaks French.

clue.text: Offence produced by very French amorous advance

parts.note: très is French for very
to make a pass at someone is to make an amorous advance

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's over-eager romantic approach gives offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a wrongdoing or sin, as in the Lord's Prayer's forgive us our trespasses.

clue.text: Complaint one never gets at home

definitions.text: Complaint one never gets at home

parts.words: Complaint one never gets at home
parts.note: a complaint can be an ailment, and this one only strikes on journeys

explanation.walkthrough: Complaint suggests grumbling; here it is an illness, and one that only affects you while on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion-induced nausea strikes passengers in cars, boats or planes, so staying put avoids it.

clue.text: Great power may — but in the past

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the past tense of the verb may

explanation.walkthrough: May could be the month; it is the modal verb, whose past form is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun denotes great strength, and the same word is the past tense of the auxiliary verb may.

clue.text: Like extended forecast for the Rockies, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covering a long period ahead, as a weather forecast
second meaning: a long mountain range, as the Rockies are

explanation.walkthrough: The Rockies are a long range of mountains, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather outlook for weeks ahead is called long-range, and the Rocky Mountains form a lengthy chain of peaks.

clue.text: Most of food in navy at sea is fish

indicators.note: in places the shortened food inside the other letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of navy are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word for food is dropped

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Sailors' meals at sea consist of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow is informal slang for food; 'Most of' drops its last letter before it is placed in the jumbled navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy is a small, strongly flavoured fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Concealment of deliveries in vessel

indicators.note: in puts the deliveries inside the vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries (balls bowled)

explanation.surface: Packages are hidden inside a container to conceal them.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled, or deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is an attempt to hide the truth or a scandal from the public.

clue.text: Never meeting obstacles in gymnastic event

parts.note: parallel lines never meet
bars are barriers or obstacles

explanation.surface: Hurdles that never meet appear in a gymnastics competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's artistic gymnastics includes an apparatus of two horizontal rails set side by side.

clue.text: Northerner in part of race covering parts of Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means the lap sits on top of the German states

parts.note: a lap is one circuit in a race
the Länder are Germany's federal states

explanation.surface: A northern runner competes in a stage of a race across German regions.
explanation.walkthrough: A Land (plural Länder) is one of Germany's federal states.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander lives in Lapland, in the far north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: One kind of mushrooms upset people, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the mushrooms are read backwards

parts.note: ceps are a variety of edible mushroom (porcini)
I is the Roman numeral one
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone unwell after eating a type of mushroom is a sample case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One kind' reads as one phrase, but 'One' gives I and 'kind of mushrooms' gives CEPS, which turned up is SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample taken as typical of its kind.

clue.text: Guns of no use at the front?

definitions.text: Guns of no use at the front?

parts.words: Guns of no use at the front?
parts.note: weapons worn at one's flank, read playfully as arms aimed sideways rather than forwards

explanation.walkthrough: The front means the battle line; weapons worn at the hip are humorously taken to point sideways, not ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and other weapons carried in a holster at the hip are called this.

clue.text: Found medicine, finally, in broken phials in city

indicators.note: in puts those two letters inside the rearranged ones
broken means the letters of the phials are smashed into a new order

parts.note: phials is plural, so two copies of the word phial

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of found and medicine

parts.note: its last letter
its last letter

explanation.surface: A drug was discovered among some smashed glass vials in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'phials' is the key: it supplies two copies of the word phial, exactly the ten letters needed around the two final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Philadelphia is a large city in Pennsylvania, USA.

clue.text: Tough love, including one kind of shock treatment

indicators.note: including means the one goes inside the other letters

parts.note: hard means tough
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Tough love is described as a form of electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock here is a thick mass of hair, so its treatment is a styling.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a bushy head of it, and a hairdo is the way it is cut and styled.

clue.text: Cherished a party on the far left

parts.note: a do is a party
red stands for the radical left in politics

explanation.surface: Someone fondly remembers a gathering held by extreme socialists.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adored is to be deeply loved and treasured.

clue.text: Makes a fuss about English, in some cases

indicators.note: in places the English abbreviation inside the cases

parts.note: crates are cases for goods

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the English language used in certain situations.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to create is to kick up a row or complain loudly.

clue.text: Series of criticisms delivered in nasal voice

indicators.note: delivered in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A barrage of complaints is spoken in a whiny, nasal tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, and figuratively a sudden barrage of attacks or criticism.

clue.text: It's difficult when Oscar, say, holds a lot of power

indicators.note: holds means the award surrounds the power letters

parts.note: an Oscar is an example of an award
KW is a kilowatt, a thousand watts of power

explanation.surface: Winning an Oscar becomes tricky when it carries great influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the radio code word for O, but it is the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awkward is hard to deal with or handle, troublesome.

clue.text: Expressed amazement, finding limited edition by poet

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English poet
ED is the shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: A collector was astonished to find a rare limited edition of a poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To marvel is to be filled with wonder and astonishment at something.

clue.text: In English elementary education, nothing that's wrong

indicators.note: In at the start says nothing goes inside the letters of elementary education

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: English primary schools teach nothing that is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The three Rs' (reading, writing and 'rithmetic) is the traditional phrase for basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, as a noun, is a mistake or fault, which is what an error is.

clue.text: Snug place to live in Sloane Street

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: Sloane Street is a smart street in Chelsea, London; the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A cosy home is advertised on a fashionable London street.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a cosy, sheltered home, used figuratively of any snug dwelling.

clue.text: Match fabric odd person appears in

indicators.note: appears in means the reworked person goes inside the fabric

parts.note: cord is corduroy fabric

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of person are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric figure turns up wearing material that clashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to agree or be equivalent, as two things that match each other.
